record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a register program that computes x^k in the non-commutative setting using only linear space and a constant number of recursive calls to x?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Give a register program for computing x k in the non-commutative setting using linear space and a constant number of recursive calls to x.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A register program is a straight-line/recursive program that manipulates values stored in a fixed collection of registers, where each register holds an element of some (possibly noncommutative) algebraic structure (e.g., elements of an associative ring or monoid, or matrices). The program may perform multiplications and assignments between registers and may recursively invoke itself on inputs. The "space" used by a computation is the total number of registers (counted with the depth of recursion) needed during execution, and a "recursive call to x" is an invocation of the program on the input x.

Problem. Working in the noncommutative setting (so the input x belongs to a noncommutative monoid/ring, and at no point may one assume xy = yx), design a register program that on input x and a positive integer k computes the power x^k, subject to the following two requirements simultaneously:
(1) the program uses only linear space in k (i.e., O(k) registers / O(k) total working space), and
(2) the program makes only a constant number (independent of k) of recursive calls on the argument x.

Either exhibit such a register program or prove that no such program exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an explicit open problem in a survey on space-reuse techniques in computation. Web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving the question of computing x^k by a register program in the noncommutative setting using linear space together with only a constant number of recursive calls to x; the status appears to remain open.
